answer: Weight climbs only while one identity keeps a relic, a record of attested work that cannot be moved to another key. The curve reaches its zenith after an unbroken run, so dividing that run across n fresh keys drops every clone to the bottom and leaves the group with about one nth of the weight. A signal is the public proof that the relic stayed on the same key. Copying it clears the run. Waiting on many keys at once does not rebuild the curve, because only consecutive epochs on one key can climb.
